fields.value: Replication Data for: Confirmation bias and misconceptions: Pupillometric evidence for a confirmation bias in misconceptions feedback

dsDescriptionValue.value: The data consists of pupillary responses to misconception feedback. We were interested in seeing how people respond to different types of feedback related to commonly held misconceptions (e.g., Napoleon was short). We measured pupil dilation in response to the feedback to see whether people respond with greater physiological reactivity to negative, ambiguous negative, positive, and ambiguous positive feedback. So, the data consists of pupil measurements and belief in misconceptions.

publicationCitation.value: Sleegers, W., Proulx, T., & van Beest, I. (2019). Confirmation bias and misconceptions: Pupillometric evidence for a confirmation bias in misconceptions feedback. Biological Psychology, 145, 76-83. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biopsycho.2019.03.018
